hook: The explorer who saw nature as one connected web, and the founder of ecology.

pages.x: Alexander von Humboldt was born in Berlin in 1769. He studied mining and worked as a mine inspector, inventing a safety lamp and a breathing mask for miners. He dreamed of exploring the tropics.

When his mother died he spent his inheritance on an expedition. In 1799 he sailed for Spanish America with the French botanist Aimé Bonpland and more than 40 instruments, landing in what is now Venezuela.

On the plains of Venezuela he wanted to study electric eels. Local men drove horses into a pool full of them; the eels attacked, stunning the horses with shocks. Humboldt got painful shocks himself and wrote it all down.
He paddled some 2,000 km up the Orinoco and its rivers, through jungle and clouds of mosquitoes, and mapped the Casiquiare, a natural channel that links the Orinoco to the Amazon.

In 1802 he climbed most of the way up Chimborazo in Ecuador, then thought the highest mountain in the world. He reached about 5,900 m, higher than anyone known before him, with bleeding gums and no oxygen.

On the mountain he saw that plants change in bands with height, just as they change from the equator to the poles, and drew it all on one famous picture. He also saw how cutting forests dried out a lake.
pages.fx: He showed nature as one connected web, the idea at the root of ecology, and was one of the first to warn that people can change the climate.

pages.x: Back in Europe he drew the first maps with isotherms, lines that join places with the same average temperature, and found that Earth's magnetism grows weaker toward the equator.
pages.fx: Weather maps still use his lines today.

pages.x: He visited Thomas Jefferson in 1804, and was said to be the most famous man in the world after Napoleon. More places, plants and animals are named after him than after almost anyone: a current, a penguin, a squid, even a sea on the Moon.
In his 70s he set out to describe the whole universe, from stars to mosses, in one work, Cosmos. He was still writing its fifth volume when he died in Berlin in 1859, aged 89.
Humboldt saw nature as one connected whole. He inspired Darwin, who said Humboldt was the reason he went exploring, and the first environmentalists.
pts: Explored South America and climbed Chimborazo
Founded the idea of nature as a web of life
Inspired Darwin and the first environmentalists
